prompts.name: 04-artisans-doorway
prompts.prompt: Use case: logo-brand. New logo concept for "KareGhar", a platform where Indian artisans are commissioned to make creative work. The client rejected a generic flower, symmetric knot, and corporate geometric K. This round must feel authored, culturally rooted and memorable. Minimalism means a small number of highly intentional shapes, not generic stock symbolism. Deliver a beautifully art-directed square logo presentation with a single primary identity, warm untextured ivory background #f6f3ec, indigo #2e3a8c and sparing burnt saffron #c2570c. Perfectly flat solid ink fills and precise edges, absolutely no gradients, no shadows, no dimensional folds. Main logo in upper middle, exact text "KareGhar" below or integrated; generous margins. At bottom show only one small monochrome version of the same mark at a plausible app-icon size. No headings, no numbered labels, no explanations, no swatches, no mockups. No flower, mandala, lotus, paisley, infinity loop or ornamental ring. Avoid generic logo-generator aesthetics. Concept: THE ARTISAN'S DOORWAY. A squat, distinctive indigo doorway silhouette inspired by the cut geometry of a traditional Indian courtyard entrance. Just two thick uneven-width jambs and a single angular stepped lintel, with a broad clear ivory opening. A small offset saffron square peeks from the lower inner edge like an open workshop shutter. The left jamb subtly curves inward like a thumb so the negative space can also suggest a maker's cupped palm: this is an understated discovery, not a literal hand illustration. Compact, slightly asymmetric, warm and monumental, like a maker's carved seal. Do not draw a whole house, roof, temple, windows, fine architectural ornament or skyline. Pair with an original softly angular, chunky lowercase wordmark spelling "kareghar" (this lowercase rendering replaces the shared casing instruction), with subtly carved terminals. Not a stock serif.

prompts.name: 05-sanjhi-kg

No flower, mandala, lotus, paisley, infinity loop or ornamental ring. Avoid generic logo-generator aesthetics. Concept: THE PAPER-CUT SIGNATURE. Create a compact custom interlocked KG letterform inspired by the positive and negative shapes of Indian Sanjhi paper cutting. A single bold irregular indigo near-square silhouette has just three decisive ivory cuts: a long narrow vertical opening, a diagonal wedge defining the K, and a generous curved counter opening sideways to define the G. Both letters share a spine; the result is a surprising ownable typographic ligature rather than two initials placed side by side. A tiny saffron offcut is displaced outside the main silhouette. Artful tension between round and sharp cuts, subtle handmade character but precise deliberate edges. No thin stencil bridges or decorative motifs. Place exact wordmark "KareGhar" in narrow clean humanist sans below, modest scale. Main symbol should dominate.

A very reduced contemporary interpretation inspired by Warli figure geometry: two small circular heads and two pairs of opposing triangular body shapes lean inward, with their short bent arms converging on one shared flat saffron work surface. Indigo figures form a compact asymmetric emblem that subtly reads as a home-shaped negative space between them, connecting artisans and customers. Use thick blunt shapes, just enough to recognize two human makers absorbed in a shared craft. Make the geometry witty, warm and unusual, with one figure slightly taller. No stick-figure dance circle, no decorative village scene, no craft tools, no extra people, no detailed hands or faces. The identity should feel like a contemporary independent Indian arts organisation. Pair with "KareGhar" in sturdy friendly custom rounded lettering, not a conventional high-contrast serif.
